newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal budget aims to cut taxes, boost investment.
newsitem.headline: Nepal budget aims to cut taxes, boost investment.

text.p: Nepal's centre-left government on Thursday presented its 1997/98 budget with proposals to cut taxes, remove obstacles to higher growth and raise investment.
The budget proposes expenditure of 62.02 billion rupees ($1.09 billion), 7.74 percent higher than the previous year. The fiscal year runs from mid-July to mid-July.

Finance Minister Rabindra Nath Sharma, unveiling the budget at a joint sitting of the two houses of parliament, said it provided fiscal incentives to encourage businessmen to step up investment in the Himalayan kingdom.
The government proposed lowering the corporate tax rate to 25 percent from 33 and income tax to 25 percent from 30.
Sharma said autonomy of the central bank was necessary for the economy to move in the right direction and added that an effective monetary policy would soon be formulated.
The Finance Minister said out of the total expenditure of 62.02 billion rupees, 37.05 billion would be raised internally.
Foreign grants from Western donors would contribute 6.02 billion rupees, while a deficit of 18.94 billion rupees ($334 million) would be met through internal and external orrowings.
The budget proposes to reduce sales tax to 10 percent from 15 and moved towards replacing the tax on contracts, hotel tax and entertainment tax with value added tax (VAT) eventually.
The government has said it would implement VAT from November despite strong protests from the business community.
Opposition members said the budget lacked innovative measures.

"Revenue projections are exaggerated and the sales tax cuts will only benefit the business sector as prices will not come down," said former finance minister and member of opposition Nepali Congress Ram Sharan Mahat.
But analysts said the overall size of the budget was within the the government's ability to implement.

"Though expenses have increased by 7.74 percent, in real terms the size of the budget is the same as the previous one if the inflation rate was to be taken into account," said Badri Prasad Shrestha, President of the Institute for Sustainable Development.
